<reason>CON kept the decisive burdens alive: Arctic inhabited sovereignty unlike Antarctica, Ilulissat 2008 rejection by necessary signatories, and Russian SSBN bastion making demilitarization unratifiable. PRO narrowed to offshore freeze and invoked 1959, but never gave a credible ratification mechanism. B answered pressure directly with CLCS/Barents 2010, title-deterrence, and Polar Code layered law, while A answered with vague deadlock-will-force-yes and reciprocal restraint.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 A1-A2 was decisive: CLCS plus bilateral precedent and no-investment-without-clear-title neutralized the Ridge-grab panic, and Polar Code plus deterrence stability showed prevention without a grand treaty, collapsing PRO's necessary-and-achievable claim.</best_rebuttal>
